decision.case_state: Routine oven repair (main element not heating, grill works). Landlord approved and Keystone Compliance assigned. A visit was booked for 30 Aug 2025 10:00-12:00, but the tenant says she agreed 8 Sept 2025 with the contractor. Ticket is on hold (Waiting for Provider) pending the contractor's confirmation of the correct date and whether anyone attended.

next_actions.action: Ask Keystone Compliance to confirm the diary date (30 Aug vs 8 Sept), whether anyone attended 30 Aug, and the correct tenant contact and attending company.
Tell the tenant the visit date is being confirmed with the contractor and that the target is within 14 days; no new appointment promised.
Hold the ticket until 1 Sept 2025 for the contractor reply; escalated for record clean-up and identity check.
Maintenance team to verify tenant identity and correct the tenant, contractor and phone records, then confirm the visit date.

boundaries: Sending messages does not confirm the visit date, that the 30 Aug visit happened or was missed, or the fault cause.
No new visit has been booked; the 8 Sept date is only the tenant's account and is unverified.
Identity of the tenant is not verified; the records name her as Ruben Oakley, Clara and Grace Mercer.
No quote, cost or landlord spend is established.
remaining_work: Contractor to confirm the correct date and whether 30 Aug was attended or missed (Keystone Compliance, by 1 Sept 2025).
Maintenance team to verify tenant identity and correct the contact and contractor records (ESC-103).
Once confirmed, book the visit with set_visit and record the outcome; then quote, repair and close as needed.
missing_info: Correct visit date (30 Aug 2025 or 8 Sept 2025).
Whether an engineer attended on 30 Aug 2025.
Verified tenant identity and correct phone number.
Correct contractor company name (Keystone Compliance, Riverside Works, Keystone Utilities or Lantern Utilities).
decision.summary: The oven repair is approved and assigned, but the visit date is disputed: the system shows 30 Aug 2025 10:00-12:00, and the tenant says she agreed 8 Sept with the contractor. I asked the contractor to confirm the diary and whether anyone attended, told the tenant the date is being checked (target within 14 days), put the ticket on hold until 1 Sept, and escalated the record conflicts (names and phone numbers) to maintenance (ESC-103).

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: Approved and assigned to Keystone Compliance, with a visit date in dispute (30 Aug 10:00-12:00 in the system vs 8 Sept per the tenant). Outstanding: the contractor's confirmation of the date and attendance, verification of the tenant's identity and records, then a booked visit, the repair and closure.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Email Keystone Compliance (existing thread) to confirm the date and attendance (A1). Email the tenant (existing thread, event 021 call) that the date is being checked, with a 14-day target (A2). Maintenance team to verify identity and records (A4, ESC-103).

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: Yes, at P3. The tenant identity and contractor and phone records conflict across the file, so a human must verify who the tenant is before any further writes or bookings. The date conflict is held until the contractor replies. No spend or safety decision is needed; the fault is routine.

args.body:
Hello,

We have a conflict on the oven repair at Flat 3, 3 Willowmere Road, Alderwick, ZZ9 6ZZ. Our records show a visit booked for this morning, Saturday 30 August 2025, 10:00-12:00. The tenant has since told us she arranged the visit for 8 September 2025 with your team.

Please reply on this thread to confirm:
1. Which date your engineer has in their diary, 30 August or 8 September 2025.
2. Whether anyone attended this morning, and if not, whether a missed-appointment has been logged.
3. The correct contact number for the tenant and the name of the company that is attending.

We will not treat the visit as confirmed until we hear back from you. Thank you.

tickets.description:
Hi there,

Hope you are well.

Apologies for bringing something to attention not long after moving in. Apart from this one small issue, everything else seems fine, and we are really enjoying the comforts of the property! :)

I am not sure if I am missing something on the fan oven. We finally managed to get around to using the oven on Tuesday evening,
(It's been a long and stressful move-in from the old place to here, so apologies for not checking this sooner).
The oven doesn't seem to heat up using the main oven section. I can confirm that the grill heating element works, as I used this last night to cook with, but the main oven heating element doesn't seem to work. On Tuesday evening, we had the oven running for at least an hour to try and get it up to 200 degrees, but it was not heating up at all.

I looked through the instruction booklet I found and am certain I am not missing anything in relation to how the oven operates.

Is this something that could be looked at, please?

Kind regards
Clara
